build:readmem-loader.notes:
Every rule was checked against the §21.4 text in t1_lrm_clean.txt. §5.7.1 covers padding and the underscore rule, and §6.8 Table 6-7 covers the x of a logic word nothing has written.

Where §21.4 does not settle a case, the model makes a choice and labels it in the UI as "the model's reading: the standard does not settle this" (basis "model"). These choices are also listed in the frame's assumptions:
(a) For a start-only call, the range that @ addresses are checked against is taken as start up to the highest address (START_ONLY_RANGE_NOTE).
(b) When loading runs past the highest address or past the finish address, or an @ address lies outside the memory with no range in the call, the model stops loading.
(c) For a sized or based number, a bad @ token or any other illegal character, the model stops at that token. The text says §21.4 forbids these but does not say how a tool reacts.
(d) Padding a short number and truncating a long one follow the sized-literal rule of §5.7.1.

The word-count warning is only checked when start and finish are both given, the file has no @ lines, and no illegal token stopped the load. It is shown as a final check step.

build:loop-tracer.notes:
What the learner gets:
- A new pure model, `src/lib/sv-loop-model.ts`. It imports `truthOf` and helpers from `sv-four-state-model` and does not change that file.
- A client component, `src/components/visuals/LoopTracer.tsx`, rendered inside VisualFrame with fidelity "model" and the assumptions list. It imports no animation library.
- Before the reveal the learner sees only the picker, the inputs and the code. They predict the pass count and the printed output, then step through the trace.
- The trace shows a flowchart (test before the body, after it, or no test, with the active box marked), the current line, loop-variable chips, a pass counter, a sim-time chip, a "statements at t = T" counter, a console, the step text with its clause, and a result line on the last step. A screen-reader live region follows each step.

How the answers are built:
- The wrong options come from re-running the model with one rule flipped. Examples: continue skips i++, break acts like continue, an x condition counts as true, signedness read the wrong way, the repeat count re-read each pass, leftmost index fastest, break leaves only the inner dimension, #5 ignored, forever runs once, a pass takes time.
- So every number and string in an option is computed by the model. A flipped rule that gives the same answer as the right one is dropped. The options are shuffled with a seed, so the answer has no fixed slot.
- The one fixed wrong option is "A run-time error stops the simulation" for repeat with a neg

build:process-tree-view.notes:
What it does: the new treeView prop draws ProcessTreeView beside the lanes. On large screens the tree takes 2fr and the lanes 3fr; on phones they stack. The tree is built from TraceStep.procs parent links, so nodes appear as you step. When a run contains disable fork, wait fork or disable <name>, the model's findTreeCheckpoints finds each such step. Playback is then held at the step before it: Next and Play are disabled there, and the scrubber, autoplay and Next are all clamped, so the kill step's narration, table and lanes cannot be seen early. The learner taps nodes (in the SVG, or with toggle buttons under it, aria-pressed and at least 40 px tall), then locks in or reveals. The reveal marks nodes ✕ killed, ⧖ waited for or ↩ forced out. It then lists every candidate node with a model-generated reason, including each miss and each extra. In tree mode the up-front PredictionPrompt is skipped, because it would give the pause's answer away. The "What to notice" line is held back until every pause is answered. Runs with no such statement, such as join-variants and event-race, keep the up-front question and still draw the tree.

Compatibility: ProcessTraceView gained two optional props, treeView and notice. Every other shared export keeps its signature. The existing six scenarios, the debug mode and the full picker are unchanged. The two new ids are offered only when named in scenario or scenarios, or by a preset. ForkJoinVisualizer now accepts ForkJoinScenarioId, which is Proces
